tagline: Out of Culpeper and up through the foothills to Chester Gap.
intro: US 522 leaves Culpeper on Evans Street and heads northwest into the Blue Ridge foothills as Sperryville Pike, through Griffinsburg, across the Hazel River and through the village of Boston. In Rappahannock County it follows Blackwater Creek through the gap between Butler Mountain and Bessie Bell Mountain to Woodville, then passes through Sperryville and crosses the Thornton River.

It runs with US 211 past the county seat of Washington, then turns north at Massies Corner as Zachary Taylor Highway, through Flint Hill and over the Jordan River and its branches, and climbs the Blue Ridge to Chester Gap, where it crosses the Appalachian Trail by the headwaters of the Rappahannock.

moments.title: Sperryville
moments.text: A village laid out in lots from 1820 on two branches of the Thornton River, which by 1880 had seven distillers and exactly one saloon.

moments.title: Washington
moments.text: Little Washington, a county seat of 86 people, whose story that George Washington surveyed it in 1749 is believed to rest on documents invented in 1932.

moments.title: Chester Gap
moments.text: At the top of the climb the highway crosses the Appalachian Trail in a wind gap of the Blue Ridge, near where the Rappahannock begins.
